properties.description: The stopping rule for the tree cap:requirement-lineage now holds (Anthony, 2026-07-25). A requirement is ATOMIC when it cannot be split further without losing meaning and one person or team can build and test it. Without a termination condition a decomposition goes wrong in BOTH directions, and the second is the dangerous one because it looks like rigour: under-decomposed leaves a compound requirement nobody can test cleanly; OVER-decomposed turns requirements into task lists and code design (\"the system must lock the account after three failed attempts\" is atomic; \"the system must query the login_attempts column and check if the integer equals 3\" is not a requirement at all). THE SIGNALS SPLIT THE SAME WAY THE QUALITY CRITERIA DO (dec:three-party-checks), which is what makes this buildable rather than advice. CHEAP AND DETERMINISTIC — build first: NO CONJUNCTIONS, a literal scan of the statement for \"and\", \"or\", \"additionally\", which is a text check needing no model and catching the most common compound requirement; SINGLE OWNER, computable from the graph as whether the capabilities satisfying it allocate to ONE component, since a leaf whose delivery is spread across several parts is not one team's to own; SINGLE TESTING POINT, partly computable as whether it has exactly one check rather than several. SEMANTIC — the agent proposes, the human decides: ESTIMABLE, and OVER-DECOMPOSED, which is the same judgement as the minimally-constrained criterion in cap:requirement-quality seen from the other end — a requirement that dictates implementation and a requirement decomposed into implementation are the same error, and noticing that they are one thing means one detector can serve both. Pairs with cap:missing-sibling: that asks whether a family is missing a member, this asks whether its members are the right SIZE, and a family of uneven grain is a signal for both. PLANNED.
properties.name: Know when to stop decomposing — and when someone went too far
